stories.title: Fifth Third, CB&T TruAmerica Lend $124M on Bay Area Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) has landed $123.5 million of construction financing to build a multifamily project in the San Francisco Bay Area, Commercial Observer has learned. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust (CB&T) provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan for the developer’s planned apartment community in San Carlos, Calif. TruAmerica Multifamily also closed a $27 million preferred equity investment to support the six-story San Mateo County development, which is slated to commence construction soon. The deal marked TruAmerica Multifamily’s first preferred equity financing since launching a structured finance platform last year. The new business vertical was formed following the addition of Ash Baraghoush, head of TruAmerica’s structured finance group, after he spent nearly a decade at Pacific Urban Investors. “This really goes hand in hand with the firm’s transformation into being a residential investment management company and being able to speak throughout the entire capital stack as opposed to just being owner operators,” Baraghoush told Commercial Observer. “We have spent a good year-plus cultivating new relationships.” Located at 11 El Camino Real 24 miles south of Downtown San Francisco, the project will feature 251 apartments with 38 of the units designated as affordable housing. Baraghoush said San Carlos has plenty of tailwinds as a multifamily market given its close ties to the San Francisco Bay Area’s technology and life science industries. He noted that the San Carlos submarket has a 97 percent multifamily occupancy rate and the region has experienced double-digit rent growth. “The Bay Area as a market has certainly outperformed and is perhaps one of the one of the better performing markets in the nation right now driven by return to office and driven by the AI boom,” Baraghoush said. “The need for affordable workforce housing continues to remain and that’s one of the attractive natures for this
bullets: Fifth Third, CB&T funded $123.5M construction loan for SummerHill/TruAmerica San Carlos apartment development.
TruAmerica closed $27M preferred equity, first deal under new structured finance platform launched 2025.
Six-story San Mateo County project commencing construction soon with full capital stack secured.
stories.summary: Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust provided a $96.5M senior construction loan for SummerHill Apartment Communities' planned apartment community in San Carlos, California. TruAmerica Multifamily also closed a $27M preferred equity investment, marking the company's first deal under its newly launched structured finance platform. The six-story San Mateo County development is poised to commence construction.
stories.impact: Bay Area multifamily financing remains active despite higher long-term borrowing costs, signaling continued capital availability for well-structured deals in supply-constrained California markets. TruAmerica's structured finance platform launch enables deeper capital stack participation, tightening equity returns but expanding deal flow—a sign lenders are pricing risk tighter as they compete for yield.

stories.title: Sports Tech Firm Genius Sports Moves U.S. HQ to Vornado’s 1290 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Sports analytics and technology company Genius Sports is relocating its U.S. headquarters to 1290 Avenue of the Americas. The London-based company’s new 10-year lease with landlord Vornado Realty Trust spans 53,000 square feet across part of the tower’s sixth floor. Asking rent was $99 per square foot, according to The Real Deal, which first reported on the lease. Newmark’s Josh Berg and A.J. Dorn negotiated the deal on behalf of Genius Sports, while Vornado was represented in-house by Ryan Levy and Edward Riguardi. A spokesperson for the landlord declined to comment on the transaction. The deal offers Genius Sports a marked expansion from its 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea offices at 512 West 22nd Street. That building changed hands last year from Vornado and the Albanese Organization to Raghsa Real Estate for $205 million. Genius Sports’ arrival brings 1290 Avenue of the Americas to 95 percent occupancy. The 43-story, full-block building between 51st and 52nd streets is anchored by investment management firm Neuberger Berman, and recently underwent a $45 million renovation that updated lobby and building amenities. Vornado owns 70 percent of the building, while the Trump Organization holds a passive 30 percent stake. Other recent arrivals at the tower include business consulting firms Portage Point Partners and Protiviti, which CO reported leased a total of 93,000 square feet late last year. In January, investment manager Oaktree leased the building’s entire 12th floor, just a few stories below law firm Selendy Gay’s 101,000-square-foot offices. Spokespeople for Genius Sports and Newmark did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Genius Sports relocates U.S. HQ to 1290 Avenue of the Americas, 53K SF at $99/SF, 10-year lease.
Expansion from 28K SF West Chelsea space signals employer growth and Manhattan office demand stabilization.
Building reaches 95% occupancy; prior tenant space sold to Raghsa for $205M in 2025.
stories.summary: Sports tech company Genius Sports signed a 10-year lease for 53,000 square feet at Vornado's 1290 Avenue of the Americas at $99 per square foot, relocating its U.S. headquarters from a 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea location. The deal brings the 43-story Midtown building to 95% occupancy. The company's prior West Chelsea building was sold to Raghsa Real Estate for $205M last year.
stories.impact: Corporate HQ growth in Midtown Manhattan signals selective recovery in office demand among stable, growing employers; however, this is offset by supply—the company abandoned 28K SF in Chelsea, which continues cycling through ownership. Multifamily developers should monitor whether Genius Sports' expansion drives incremental worker population to Midtown submarkets or simply consolidates existing workforce, which affects residential demand timing.

stories.title: Data Center Developer Increases Land Holdings at Briscoe County Site
stories.excerpt: Soluna Holdings, a developer of green data centers for intensive computing applications, including AI and Bitcoin mining, closed the purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas. The land will host Project Dorothy 3, Soluna’s planned renewable-first AI computing campus with a potential capacity of up to 300 MW. Briscoe County is between Amarillo and Lubbock. The parcel sits adjacent to Projects Dorothy 1 and 2 and to the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm, which Soluna acquired in April. The Briscoe Wind Farm’s Substation sits directly across from the acquired property, positioning Dorothy 3 for direct, behind-the-meter access to generation the Company owns outright.  The 397 acres exceed the 300 acres Soluna originally identified for the campus. The additional land gives the Company room to add data halls should further generation or storage capacity become available at the site.  Project Dorothy 3 is part of Soluna’s development pipeline of approximately 6.3 GW across multiple sites. Soluna currently operates approximately 192 MW of energized capacity.  The post Data Center Developer Increases Land Holdings at Briscoe County Site appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Soluna Holdings acquired 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas for Project Dorothy 3 AI data center campus.
Facility will support up to 300 MW capacity; 150 MW wind farm and substation already owned on adjacent land.
Exceeds original 300-acre plan, providing buffer for future data hall expansion with grid access locked in.
stories.summary: Data center developer Soluna Holdings closed purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas (between Amarillo and Lubbock) for Project Dorothy 3, a planned renewable-first AI computing campus with capacity up to 300 MW. The parcel sits adjacent to Soluna's existing Projects Dorothy 1 and 2 and a 150 MW wind farm acquired in April, providing direct behind-the-meter generation access. The extra 97 acres beyond the original 300-acre plan allow room for additional data halls.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact, but hyperscale AI/data center development in remote Texas regions will drive demand for worker housing in Briscoe County and nearby towns (Silverton, Quitaque) if local labor cannot cover operations. Soluna's 6.3 GW pipeline suggests sustained infrastructure investment; this could indirectly support small-market multifamily demand near data centers if workforce in-migration occurs—monitor employment announcements.

stories.title: SJC Ventures Sells Whole Foods-Anchored Center in South Florida for $83M
stories.excerpt: SJC Ventures has sold a newly completed Whole Foods-anchored retail center in Doral, Fla., for $83 million, property records show. Called Doral Marketplace, the property spans 89,000 square feet at 10800 Northwest 41st Street, about a mile east of the Florida Turnpike and 14 miles west of Downtown Miami. Atlanta-based SJC Ventures completed the 10-acre strip mall last quarter. The sale excluded a 1.8-acre portion of the property leased to Chick-fil-A. Records list the buyer as Traditions Management, a Dallas-based developer and operator of senior living communities. The buyer assumed a loan with $50 million in outstanding debt, which has now been assigned to the Bank of Texas. Whole Foods is Doral Marketplace’s biggest tenant with a 43,000-square-foot location. Other tentants include J. Crew Factory, Ulta Beauty, Shake Shack, First Watch, GoodVets, The Spot Barbershop, Encore Nails, VIO MedSpa and Apizza Brooklyn Resto + Vino. The sale comes as Miami-Dade County retail leasing remains strong. During the second quarter of 2026, average asking rents jumped to $42.50 per square foot, up 2.6 percent quarter-over-quarter, while the vacancy rate fell to 3 percent. More than 1.3 million square feet of retail space remains under construction, including another Whole Foods location in South Beach, for which developer Russell Galbut nabbed a $54 million construction loan last year. Representatives for SJC Ventures and Traditions Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SJC Ventures sold Doral Marketplace, 89K SF Whole Foods-anchored center, to Traditions Management for $83M.
Buyer assumed $50M loan; sale excludes 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A parcel; Miami-Dade retail rents jumped 2.6% YoY to $42.50/SF Q2 2026.
Buyer is Dallas-based senior living developer—signals retail-to-residential conversion opportunity or diversification strategy in South Florida.
stories.summary: SJC Ventures sold Doral Marketplace, a newly completed 89,000-square-foot Whole Foods-anchored strip center in Doral, Florida, for $83 million to Dallas-based Traditions Management, a senior living developer and operator. The buyer assumed a $50M loan (now assigned to Bank of Texas); the sale excluded a 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A parcel. Miami-Dade County retail leasing remains strong, with average asking rents at $42.50/SF in Q2 2026, up 2.6% year-over-year.
stories.impact: Acquisition by senior living operator signals potential future value-add conversion play (retail-to-residential or mixed-use) in Doral, a high-growth West Miami submarket. Strong retail leasing (2.6% YoY rent growth) reflects underlying demand; if Traditions executes retail conversion or adds multifamily, it indicates Doral's trajectory supports higher-density residential. Multifamily developers should monitor Doral/west Miami-Dade for available land and retail conversion opportunities given population growth and constrained supply.

stories.title: KeyBank Expands to 113K SF at Elecor’s 1301 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: A major banking institution has added 15,292 square feet to its Manhattan office footprint, Commercial Observer has learned. Keybank signed a 15-year deal to renew its existing space and expand to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties’ 1301 Avenue of the Americas across the entire 35th, 36th and 37th floors, as well as portions of the 28th and 38th floors, according to the landlord. Neye, Elecor’s senior vice president of leasing, added in a statement that the lease demonstrates the “enduring appeal of a high-quality, well-located workplace.” Other tenants in the building between West 52nd and West 53rd streets include investment bank Piper Sandler, which signed a lease for 140
bullets: KeyBank expanded to 112.9K SF across five floors at 1301 Avenue of the Americas, 15-year renewal + expansion deal.
Midtown office asking rents averaged $86.18/SF Q2 2026; KeyBank's expansion signals major bank commitment to Manhattan.
Employer footprint growth in core Plaza District—indirect indicator of office labor demand and potential housing proximity needs.
stories.summary: KeyBank signed a 15-year lease to renew and expand its Manhattan office footprint to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties' 1301 Avenue of the Americas, occupying the entire 35th, 36th, and 37th floors plus portions of the 28th and 38th floors. The Plaza District tower's average asking rent in Midtown for Q2 2026 was $86.18/SF. The expansion adds 15,292 square feet to the bank's existing space.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance—office lease activity does not consistently translate to residential demand in Manhattan given long commuting patterns and existing high housing density. However, KeyBank's large-footprint expansion signals confidence in NYC office market durability, which may stabilize employer retention and reduce downside risk to Manhattan residential submarkets that depend on stable professional employment.

stories.title: League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space
stories.excerpt: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on the $78 million mixed-use business park Lilac Field in League City. The development is seeking its first industrial and retail tenants. Located between League City Parkway and SH 146, Lilac Field will span 24.5 acres and include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space. Community Impact reports once complete, Lilac Field will include 16 small warehouse units and seven retail and restaurant buildings, with warehouse tenants expected to include entertainment venues, gyms, childcare providers and breweries. The development’s first two industrial buildings are expected to be completed by early 2027. The developer is seeking industrial clients, such as aerospace and aviation suppliers, marine service groups, technology firms, energy service companies, advanced manufacturing users and specialty distributors to rent its warehouse space. The full buildout is projected to take three to five years. The post League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on $78M Lilac Field mixed-use business park in League City, Texas.
Project spans 24.5 acres: 70K SF retail/restaurant, 220K SF flexible warehouse (16 small units, 7 retail buildings).
First two industrial buildings due early 2027; seeking aerospace, aviation, tech, marine, advanced manufacturing tenants.
stories.summary: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on Lilac Field, a $78 million mixed-use business park in League City, Texas, located between League City Parkway and SH 146. The 24.5-acre development will include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space across 16 small warehouse units and seven retail/restaurant buildings. First two industrial buildings are expected to be completed by early 2027.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; however, Lilac Field's targeted tenants (aerospace, aviation, marine, advanced manufacturing, tech) drive job creation in the League City submarket. If successful, sustained industrial and small-business growth will increase worker population, eventually supporting multifamily demand in League City proper. Monitor absorption pace and tenant announcements to gauge timing for residential development in this Houston exurb.

stories.title: Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Developer Naseem Shaik is moving forward on a $240 million Prosper project that will include a hotel, offices, retail and restaurants. No multifamily is planned at the time. Dubbed Bella Prosper, it will sit on 61 acres with a large manmade lake in the middle. The development will incorporate one-story offices as well as office space above restaurant and retail spaces. Features of Bella Prosper include a 139-key hotel geared toward business travelers, a public parking deck and a park with a water feature. Bella Prosper is slated to build at least 60,950 square feet of retail space. Community Impact reports Bella Prosper is expected to create $59.8 million in annual taxable sales. Developers estimate that Bella Prosper as a whole will generate $88.3 million in net benefits for the town over the next 25 years. Construction on Phase 1 was originally expected to start in late 2027. The post Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Developer Naseem Shaik planning $240M Bella Prosper mixed-use project: 139-key hotel, office, retail, restaurants, no multifamily.
61-acre site includes public park, lake feature, 60,950 SF retail; Phase 1 construction originally planned late 2027.
Estimated $88.3M net benefits over 25 years; no residential component signals hotel and office priority in Prosper market.
stories.summary: Developer Naseem Shaik is advancing Bella Prosper, a $240 million mixed-use development on 61 acres in Prosper, Texas, featuring a 139-key business-travel hotel, office space, retail (60,950 SF), and restaurants, with a manmade lake and public park. Phase 1 construction was originally scheduled to start in late 2027. The project includes no multifamily component at this time and is projected to generate $88.3 million in net benefits for the town over 25 years.
stories.impact: Mixed-use development without multifamily signals developer confidence in Prosper's office/hospitality demand but not residential absorption, suggesting housing supply may be adequate or demand signals favor hotel/office over apartments. Developers should monitor Bella Prosper's tenant mix and absorption; if office/hotel underperform, it may indicate softer job growth in North Dallas and weaker rental demand, lowering multifamily feasibility in Prosper submarket.

stories.title: Retail Leads as CRE Recovery Diverges Across Sectors, Markets
stories.excerpt: The U.S. commercial real estate recovery is following markedly different paths across property sectors and markets, Integra Realty Resources (IRR) said in its newly released 2026 Mid-Year Viewpoint Report. More than 90% of retail markets surveyed are in recovery or expansion, while office markets remain evenly divided between recovery and recession. Multifamily performance is shaped largely by local supply cycles, while industrial markets are concentrated primarily in the expansion and hypersupply phases. Across all four sectors, IRR’s data show a continued flight to quality, with modern, well-located and specialized properties outperforming older or commodity-oriented assets. Meanwhile, speculative construction has slowed sharply. “National data provide essential context, but the clearest picture emerges when it is informed by what is happening on the ground,” said IRR CEO Anthony M. Graziano. “Investors cannot assume that modest rate cuts will meaningfully improve transaction economics, particularly while long-term borrowing costs and equity return requirements remain elevated. Through year-end and into 2027, we expect opportunities to remain concentrated in markets and assets where the basis, income growth and local demand support the investment case.” The post Retail Leads as CRE Recovery Diverges Across Sectors, Markets appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Integra Realty Resources 2026 Mid-Year report: 90%+ retail markets in recovery/expansion; office markets evenly split recovery/recession.
Multifamily shaped by local supply cycles; industrial concentrated in expansion/hypersupply phases; speculative construction sharply slowed.
Sector divergence and flight-to-quality signal investors cannot assume modest rate cuts improve underwriting; equity return requirements remain elevated through 2027.
stories.summary: Integra Realty Resources' 2026 Mid-Year Viewpoint Report found that more than 90% of retail markets surveyed are in recovery or expansion, while office markets remain evenly divided between recovery and recession. Multifamily performance is shaped largely by local supply cycles, industrial markets are concentrated in expansion and hypersupply, and speculative construction has slowed sharply. A continued flight to quality favors modern, well-located, and specialized properties over older or commodity assets.
stories.impact: Critical strategic signal: sector divergence persists, favoring retail and well-operated multifamily in tight supply markets but pressuring office and overbuilt industrial. Elevated equity return requirements and unchanged long-term borrowing costs mean deal feasibility depends entirely on basis, income growth, and local demand—not macro rate cuts. Developers should focus capital on supply-constrained metros with demonstrated rent growth, avoid speculative starts, and discount rate-cut benefits. Flight-to-quality will continue pressuring Class B/C multifamily and favoring premium assets.

stories.title: Mac Cosmetics’ SoHo Flagship Relocates to 5K SF at 579 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Mac Cosmetics has selected a new foundation in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The global makeup brand signed a 5,325-square-foot lease at 579 Broadway between Prince and East Houston streets to host its next flagship location in the trendy shopping corridor, according to an announcement from landlord broker Newmark. The deal represents a relocation of just two blocks from Mac’s current perch alongside Bloomingdale’s at 506 Broadway. The landlord at 579 Broadway, Lord Shivas Properties, was represented by Newmark’s Ariel Schuster, Michael Paster and Logan Ryan. Paster said in a statement that the location, neighbored by brands like jewelry brand Pandora and bohemian clothing store Free People Movement, was a “natural fit for Mac Cosmetics.” The brand plans to occupy approximately 3,825 square feet on the ground floor and 1,500 square feet of lower-level space within the five-story building. The length of Mac’s lease and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from CBRE found retail rents near SoHo’s Prince Street averaged $1,408 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026. Mac will take possession of the storefront in January, according to Newmark. Its current occupant, British fashion retailer AllSaints, will occupy the space through the end of the year. A spokesperson for AllSaints did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its future plans in the neighborhood. Cushman & Wakefield’s Mike O’Neill, Jason Greenstone and Taylor Reynolds negotiated the lease on behalf of Mac Cosmetics. The lease offered Mac the opportunity to secure a highly visible location in the corridor, O’Neill told CO in a statement. “We’re pleased to have helped facilitate a transaction that aligns Mac with a location well positioned to support its long-term retail objectives,” O’Neill said. Lord Shivas Properties also owns the lot’s adjacent storefront at 152 Mercer Street, the site of luxury knitwear brand Extreme Cashmere‘s U.S. flagship. Emily
bullets: MAC Cosmetics relocated SoHo flagship two blocks within neighborhood, 5.3K SF lease at 579 Broadway between Prince and Houston.
Relocated from 506 Broadway (Bloomingdale's co-tenancy); ground floor 3.8K SF, lower level 1.5K SF; neighbors include Pandora, Free People.
Retail rents in SoHo remain elevated; flagship relocation signals strength in luxury retail corridor but no material multifamily impact.
stories.summary: MAC Cosmetics signed a 5,325-square-foot lease at 579 Broadway in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood to host its flagship location, relocating two blocks from its current space at 506 Broadway. The brand will occupy approximately 3,825 square feet on the ground floor and 1,500 square feet of lower-level space in the five-story building, anchored by Pandora and Free People Movement. The lease terms were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance—luxury retail leasing in SoHo reflects consumer spending and tourism strength in lower Manhattan, but flagship relocations do not drive residential demand. SoHo remains supply-constrained for multifamily; any developer interest should focus on transit-proximate, mixed-use conversion opportunities rather than relying on retail tenant activity.

stories.title: Vintage Phoenix Midrise Office Building Slated for Hotel Rooms
stories.excerpt: The building is nearly a 100 years old, but that isn’t stopping Phoenix developers CivicGroup and Sunflower Development from converting the onetime office tower into hotel rooms. Built in 1928, the Security Building will undergo a $135 million renovation that will include 255 hotel rooms. In addition to the hotel rooms, the redevelopment will include 15,000 square feet of meeting space – including the 5,500-square-foot 1928 ballroom – and other amenities. The investor duo hopes to open five food-and-beverage outlets in the hotel, including multiple bars, a three-meal restaurant, and an upscale eatery. The building is currently owned by Maricopa County and will continue to lease the building to the development team as a hotel for at least 20 years. The Phoenix Business Journal reports the project requires a significant amount of preservation work – including the removal of drywall, carpet, non-historic walls and cubicles. The developers hope to start in the first quarter of 2027 and open in Q4 2028. The post Vintage Phoenix Midrise Office Building Slated for Hotel Rooms appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Phoenix CivicGroup and Sunflower Development converting 1928 Security Building (office) to 255-room hotel via $135M renovation.
Building owned by Maricopa County, leased to developers for 20+ years; includes 15K SF meeting space, five F&B outlets.
Construction start Q1 2027, opening Q4 2028—signals Phoenix office-to-hotel conversion viability; no multifamily component.
stories.summary: CivicGroup and Sunflower Development are converting Phoenix's 1928 Security Building, a historic office tower, into a 255-room hotel through a $135 million renovation. The project includes 15,000 square feet of meeting space (including a 5,500-square-foot ballroom) and five food-and-beverage outlets. The County of Maricopa owns the building and will lease it to the development team as a hotel for at least 20 years. Construction is targeted for Q1 2027 with an opening by Q4 2028.
stories.impact: Historic office-to-hotel conversion signals weak Phoenix downtown office absorption and developer confidence in hotel demand, but no multifamily upside. Conversion removes potential future multifamily-in-conversion opportunity. Monitor whether similar Phoenix CBD office stock converts to residential or hotel—if hotel dominates, it suggests office oversupply but weak housing demand signals, reducing downtown residential development feasibility.
